newsitem.title: USA: British man faces NJ fraud scheme charges.
newsitem.headline: British man faces NJ fraud scheme charges.

text.p: A British man has been extradited to the United States from Switzerland to face a hearing on charges that he conspired with others to defraud investors of $4.32 million, officials said on Wednesday.

U.S. Attorney Faith Hochberg of New Jersey said in a statement that 53-year-old David Dunn was allegedly involved in a bogus trust named the Euro-American Money Fund Trust. A New Jersey man controlled its interests in the United States.
Dunn, whose home is in Geneva, Switzerland, was extradited to the United States on January 9 after his appeal of the extradition order was denied by the Swiss Supreme Court.

His arraignment was scheduled for Thursday on charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud. He was indicted by a grand jury in January last year and Dunn had been detained in a Swiss prison since March.

The victims of the alleged fraud were Ingo-Pet, a German company that was acting in partnership with a Russian company called Ljukon. They were induced to pay a $4.32 million advance fee in order to buy what Dunn and his co-conspirators called a "Master Collateral Commitment", the statement said.

According to Dunn's indictment, John Voigt, formerly of Linwood, New Jersey, was a director of Euro-American who controlled operations in the United States. Voigt was convicted in 1994 with two other people in New Jersey and is serving a 15-year sentence in a federal jail.
